candidates.title: OpenStax worked reading: y = −3(x + 2)^2 + 4
candidates.student_facing: The equation is y = −3(x + 2)^2 + 4. Name the vertex, say whether the graph has a maximum or a minimum, and say how you knew.
candidates.source_stem: OpenStax calls a(x − h)^2 + k standard form and also vertex form; Ontario calls that expression vertex form. Keep OpenStax wording in source fields; do not rename in student prose without the Ontario note.
candidates.answer: The vertex is at (−2, 4). Because a < 0, the parabola opens downward (vertex is a maximum). h = −2 because x − h = x + 2.
candidates.answer_verification: Copied from OpenStax College Algebra 2e §5.1 worked text on m51274 (Figure 5 paragraph).

provenance.attribution: OpenStax College Algebra 2e, Quadratic Functions (m51274). CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. https://openstax.org/details/books/college-algebra-2e

candidates.title: OpenStax verbal: another name for their standard form
candidates.student_facing: OpenStax writes a quadratic as f(x) = a(x − h)^2 + k and calls that writing standard form. What other name does OpenStax give that same writing?
candidates.source_stem: OpenStax uses “standard form” for a(x − h)^2 + k and also calls it vertex form. Ontario uses vertex form for that expression and standard form for ax^2 + bx + c. Keep the OpenStax naming in the stem; add the Ontario note in teacher copy only. Source: College Algebra 2e §5.1 Verbal #4.
candidates.answer_verification: OpenStax §5.1 states that because the vertex appears in f(x) = a(x − h)^2 + k, that writing is also known as the vertex form of a quadratic function. Verbal exercise 4 asks for another name for their standard form.

provenance.attribution: OpenStax College Algebra 2e, Quadratic Functions (m51274) §5.1 Verbal #4. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. https://openstax.org/details/books/college-algebra-2e

candidates.title: OpenStax verbal: advantage of this form
candidates.student_facing: This writing of a quadratic is f(x) = a(x − h)^2 + k. What can you read from it that is harder to see when the same function is written as ax^2 + bx + c?
candidates.source_stem: Do not call a(x − h)^2 + k “standard form” in student prose without the Ontario naming note. OpenStax source stem uses “standard form” for vertex form.
candidates.answer: When written in that form, the vertex can be easily identified.
